title: The Insurance Company That Hired Hitmen to Kill Policyholders
hook: They collected premiums for years, then sent a man to make sure you never collected your payout.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines true crime with corporate evil, a rare documented case of a company literally killing its own customers.

title: The Trader Who Manipulated a Tsunami Warning to Crash Oil Futures
hook: He faked a government alert from a stolen satellite signal—and made $400 million in 12 minutes.
why_this_can_go_viral: Feels like a spy thriller plot, but it's real—exploiting fear of natural disaster to move markets.

title: The Startup That Sold Your DNA to Insurers—Without Telling You
hook: You spit in a tube for 'genetic ancestry.' They sold your data to life insurers who raised your rates.
why_this_can_go_viral: Personal and terrifying—everyone who used a home DNA kit could be affected; taps into privacy paranoia.

title: The Monopoly That Bought Every Parking Garage in America
hook: Then they raised rates 300% and lobbied cities to fine you for parking anywhere else.
why_this_can_go_viral: Relatable frustration—everyone hates parking fees; revealing it's a deliberate monopoly fuels outrage.

title: The Spy Who Infiltrated a Chocolate Factory to Steal the Cocoa Recipe
hook: He posed as a flavor scientist for 18 months, then vanished with the secret blend—and the company collapsed.
why_this_can_go_viral: Deliciously dramatic—food secrets are universally tantalizing, and the spy story is cinematic.

title: The Ad Agency That Sneaked Subliminal Earworm Jingles Into Songs
hook: They paid pop artists to insert 1-second audio commands—you couldn't hear them, but your brain bought products.
why_this_can_go_viral: Paranoid and fascinating—everyone will wonder if their favorite song made them buy something.

title: The Factory That Mixed Sawdust Into Bread Flour—For 20 Years
hook: It was called 'fiber enrichment.' Actually, it was just wood pulp—and it passed every health inspection.
why_this_can_go_viral: Gross-out shock factor—people love to be disgusted by what they eat; bread is a daily staple.

title: The Pharma Company That Sold Placebo Chemo—Knew It Was Sugar
hook: Patients 'took' chemotherapy in a pill—it was just sugar and dye—and the CEO called it 'cost-effective.'
why_this_can_go_viral: Extreme moral outrage—people dying from fake cancer treatment; triggers viral anger and sharing.

title: The Trader Who Used a Prison Inmate's Phone to Front-Run Trades
hook: He bribed a guard to smuggle a smartphone into a federal prison—so an inmate could call in market tips.
why_this_can_go_viral: Absurd and unbelievable—a trader inside prison still manipulating Wall Street; feels like a movie.

title: The Startup That Built a Fake City to Attract Investors
hook: They rented abandoned buildings, hired 200 actors, and staged a 'vibrant tech hub'—investors poured in millions.
why_this_can_go_viral: Visual spectacle—imagine a whole fake town; shares like a jaw-dropping heist story.

title: The Monopoly That Owns All the Cemeteries—Charges Rent for Your Grave
hook: You buy a plot, but they own the dirt. Miss a payment? They dig you up and sell the spot again.
why_this_can_go_viral: Morbid, shocking, universally relevant—everyone dies; the idea of being evicted from your grave is terrifying.

title: The Ad Agency That Created a Fake Virus—to Sell Disinfectant
hook: They hired actors to cough in subways, planted 'health alerts' online—then launched a cleaning product that 'cured' it.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exploits pandemic-era fears; feels like a conspiracy theory but it's documented—high outrage and shareability.

title: The Factory That Sold 'Vegan' Meat—It Was Ground Chicken With Green Dye
hook: Lab tests revealed 100% poultry. The label said '100% plant-based.' The CEO said, 'Close enough.'
why_this_can_go_viral: Betrayal of vegan consumers—dual audience outrage (vegans and meat-eaters both feel conned).

title: The Corp That Bought a News Channel—Then Used It to Destroy a Rival's CEO
hook: They ran 400 negative segments in 30 days. The rival's stock crashed. The news channel denied everything.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exposes media corruption—people already distrust news; this confirms their worst suspicions.

title: The Trader Who Faked His Own Death—Twice—to Avoid Margin Calls
hook: He jumped off a bridge in 2008—but was seen trading from a café in 2009. The second time, they found him.
why_this_can_go_viral: Audacious and unbelievable—faking death twice is pure clickbait gold; feels like a crime drama.

title: The Startup That Hired Ghosts—Then Sold Shares in Dead People
hook: They recruited homeless people, registered them as employees, then took out life insurance policies—and waited.
why_this_can_go_viral: Morally repugnant, unbelievable—turns the 'startup hustle' into a murder conspiracy; goes viral on shock alone.

title: The Monopoly That Bought All the Light Bulbs—Then Made Them Burn Out in 1 Year
hook: They secretly designed the bulbs to fail—so you'd keep buying. It's called 'planned obsolescence.' And it's legal.
why_this_can_go_viral: Classic revelation that makes people angry about everyday products—high education + outrage.

title: The Spy Who Seduced a CEO—Then Stole His Company's Formula for Shampoo
hook: A corporate spy married a billionaire, got access to the lab, and handed the formula to a competitor—for $50 million.
why_this_can_go_viral: Juicy, scandalous—spy romance and betrayal; feels like a Netflix documentary trailer.

title: The Ad Agency That Used a Fake Funeral to Sell Life Insurance
hook: They staged a widow crying over a casket in a public square. The 'dead husband' was an actor. The real product? Annuities.
why_this_can_go_viral: Manipulative and grotesque—people love to hate fake emotional stunts; triggers moral disgust.

title: The Factory That Sold 'Fresh' Eggs—They Were 3 Years Old, Coated in Mineral Oil
hook: Eggs were labeled 'farm fresh'—but they came from a warehouse silo, coated in oil, and had zero expiration date.
why_this_can_go_viral: Grocery staple betrayal—everyone buys eggs; the gross-out factor drives shares.

title: The Oil Company That Bought a University—Then Changed the Science Textbooks
hook: They funded a climate department, then rewrote the curriculum to call CO2 'plant food.' Graduates never learned the truth.
why_this_can_go_viral: Extreme—buying a whole university to shape science; triggers massive debate and sharing among climate-aware audiences.

title: The Trader Who Used a Weather Balloon to Predict Crop Yields—Before Satellites
hook: He launched a secret balloon over Kansas in 1983, saw the drought first, and shorted wheat futures—before anyone else could blink.
why_this_can_go_viral: Clever and retro-tech—people love underdog hacks; feels like a forgotten genius move.

title: The Corp That Bought a Town's Water—Then Billed Residents for Rain
hook: They owned the rights to all groundwater. When it rained, they charged homeowners for 'using' it—off their own roofs.
why_this_can_go_viral: Infuriating and absurd—billing for rainwater feels dystopian; triggers outrage and environmental sharing.

title: The Monopoly That Bought All the Ladders—Then Charged $500 to Rent One
hook: They owned 90% of ladder production in the US. Then they lobbied for a law requiring safety-certified ladders—only theirs passed.
why_this_can_go_viral: Absurd everyday item—people can't believe they're being ripped off for something so simple; high frustration shareability.
